subject: Peakiq: temporary p95 weighting & regional measurement window amendment request
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@peakiq.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Reed <marcus@peakiq.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary p95 weighting & regional window during migration

David —

Thanks again for the sync this morning. Quick follow-up from our infra team: Peakiq will be doing a rolling data-center migration next Thursday through Saturday (US-west). We expect an increase in short-lived spikes as traffic shifts during the cutover (estimated 6–12 hours of elevated tail latency each day).

Given that, we'd like to request a temporary adjustment to the Hosted API latency SLO measurement for our account while the migration is underway. Specifically: 
- Temporarily apply a weighted p95 that discounts short-lived peak periods (you suggested a daypart carveout during the call).
- Restrict the measurement window for p95 to regional buckets (US-west) for the migration period.

We know this is an unusual ask. Our goals are: avoid a credit trigger for transient migration noise, and make sure our production users maintain acceptable UX expectations.

Can Redwood propose an operational footing (exact wording for the contract addendum + evidence we should provide)? Marcus and I can share the migration timeline and sample dashboards.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Park
Head of Infrastructure, Peakiq
[t] +1 415 555 0198

Attachment: peakiq-migration-timeline.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@peakiq.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Reed <marcus@peakiq.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary p95 weighting & regional window during migration

Elena —

Appreciate the heads-up. I've looped in Marissa (Customer Success lead on the account) and Lauren from Reliability to scope the operational change and required evidence. High-level answer: we can support a temporary measurement adjustment for the migration period, provided we document the window, the exact carveout criteria, and gating evidence (traffic patterns + post-migration validation).

Proposed approach (quick draft):
1) Amendment duration: 48–72 hours (covering planned cutover + a 24h stabilization window).
2) Measurement change: apply a regional p95 measurement that excludes short-lived peak intervals defined as contiguous 15-minute windows where 95th suffers >2x baseline and the incident is less than 12 hours total.
3) Evidence required from Peakiq before amendment: migration timeline, expected maintenance windows, and a pre-cutover baseline p50/p95 dashboard.
4) Post-migration validation: after the window, Redwood will run a 72-hour rolling comparison; if p95 regressions persist outside of expected noise, the amendment may be revoked.

Marissa — can you draft an amendment bullet to send to legal and provide the exact consumer-facing wording (credits / non-credit trigger language)? Lauren — can we pre-configure a regional measurement slice for Peakiq so the change is operationally small?

I'll package the proposal and a lightweight evidence checklist for Elena to sign off on.

Best,
David Kim
Principal Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Note: forwarding peakiq-migration-timeline.xlsx to our legal/dispute folder for reference.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@peakiq.com>, Marcus Reed <marcus@peakiq.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 08:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary p95 weighting & regional window during migration

David / Lauren —

Draft amendment language below (lean; legal review needed). Elena / Marcus — flag anything that looks off and we'll iterate.

--- Amendment (draft) ---
For the migration window defined in the attached timeline, Redwood Inference will apply a temporary regional measurement adjustment to the Hosted API latency SLO applicable to Peakiq (Deal PEAQ-4721). The adjustment will: 
• Be effective for the dates/times agreed in writing and not exceed 72 hours in total.
• Compute p95 for Redwood-hosted endpoints serving Peakiq traffic using a regional (US-west) measurement slice during the effective period.
• Exclude short-lived contiguous 15-minute sub-windows that meet the following criteria: the instantaneous p95 exceeds 2x Peakiq baseline p95 and the total contiguous outage window is less than 12 hours.
• Be conditioned on receipt of Peakiq-provided evidence: migration timeline, pre-cutover baseline dashboard, and post-cutover confirmation.
• Not constitute a waiver of any underlying SLA beyond the narrow measurement adjustment described above; normal SLA terms and credits continue to apply outside the effective period.

---

Attachments to include with request: p95-evidence-dashboard.pdf (exports of baseline dashboards), signed timeline (peakiq-migration-timeline.xlsx).

If you approve I'll route this to Legal and add a one-paragraph DocuSign amendment for signature.

Marissa
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Attachment: p95-evidence-dashboard.pdf (PDF stub)

From: Elena Park <elena.park@peakiq.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Reed <marcus@peakiq.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Aug 2026 16:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary p95 weighting & regional window during migration

Marissa / David —

Thanks, this looks good and aligned with what we discussed. Marcus and I reviewed the draft and have two small asks: 
1) Extend the stabilization window to 36 hours (instead of 24) to cover rollback testing.
2) Add a short clause that commits Redwood to provide a raw event export (CSV of tail latency samples) on request within 72 hours if the amendment is invoked — Peakiq will use this for internal analysis only.

If you can fold those in, we can sign the amendment today — will route via DocuSign after legal quick review.

—Elena
Elena Park
Head of Infrastructure, Peakiq
